fact: Motz, an infill maker, says low infill depth is the main reason artificial turf fibers flatten and stop standing up, and names two causes: installers who put down too little infill, and infill that settles or is displaced over time, especially where kids and pets run.
quote: The main reason turf fibers flatten and lose the ability to “stand” vertically like natural grass does is low turf infill depth. … Often, installers don’t add enough infill to brand-new turf systems. … Infill levels naturally settle and material can be displaced over time, especially in highly trafficked areas of your yard. Have kids or pets? Small running feet and paws are known to move infill around.
source_label: The Motz Group, How to Get Turf Fibers in Artificial Grass to Stand Up Tall When They're Flat (May 27, 2021)
notes: Motz makes and sells Envirofill and SafeShell infill, so it has a stake in infill-first advice. Read in full with curl on 2026-09-25.

fact: Motz says turf without enough infill to hold the fibers up is more prone to blades breaking and fraying and far more likely to mat, and that matted turf can look shiny and artificial.
quote: Without turf infill to help the fibers stand up, turf is more prone to blades breaking and fraying, and it’s also a lot more likely to become matted. … With artificial grass, that matted-down effect can make your turf’s surface appear shiny and, well, artificial.
source_label: The Motz Group, How to Get Turf Fibers in Artificial Grass to Stand Up Tall When They're Flat (May 27, 2021)

fact: Motz says bulky or heavy objects left in one place on turf for long periods flatten it and leave imprints, and advises moving them around often and filling infill to the top of the fibers where furniture will sit.
quote: And if you leave bulky or heavy objects in the same place over extended periods, it will cause the turf to lay flat, and the objects will leave imprints. The best practice is to move objects around on the turf frequently to prevent flattening and to fill your infill to the top of the turf fibers in areas where the furniture will be placed.
source_label: The Motz Group, How to Get Turf Fibers in Artificial Grass to Stand Up Tall When They're Flat (May 27, 2021)

fact: Motz recommends a stiff brush or a power broom with nylon bristles to lift flat turf: a power broom for a whole backyard, heavy matting or compacted infill; a Grandi Groom rake as the middle option for medium lawns and routine upkeep; and a manual brush for small areas and spot fixes, such as where a lawn chair sat.
quote: To help your turf fibers stand at attention, use a stiff brush or artificial grass power broom with nylon bristles across your artificial turf surface. … Power broom: A power broom is ideal for large turf applications, like an entire backyard that needs to be revived. If your turf fibers are heavily matted or if your infill has become compacted, a power broom provides the necessary force to rejuvenate your turf … Grandi Groom: More efficient than a manual brush but with a bit less horsepower than a power broom, a Grandi Groom is a good middle-path option. They’re useful for medium-sized lawns and for regular upkeep, as well as for redistributing infill and lifting turf fibers in high-traffic areas. Brush: A manual brush is perfect for smaller areas and spot treatments, such as lifting back up flat artificial grass after a lawn chair has rested on it.
source_label: The Motz Group, How to Get Turf Fibers in Artificial Grass to Stand Up Tall When They're Flat (May 27, 2021)

fact: Motz's steps for flat turf, to be done at least once a year: brush against the grain first, then in all directions; afterward, pressed blades should spring straight back, and a spot that stays flat likely needs more infill.
quote: To fix flattened fake grass, try the following, and make these steps a proactive part of your artificial turf backyard’s care at least once a year. … As you do this, brush or drag your chosen tool against the grain of the fibers first to help lift them and allow more infill to get securely to the base. Then, brush in all different directions to give your outdoor artificial grass a natural and fluffed-up look and to ensure the infill is evenly distributed. … The turf fibers should feel relatively stiff and resilient, and if you press down lightly on them, the blades should bounce back up immediately when you release pressure. If you do this and are left with flat artificial grass in that spot, or if some areas of your turf system still appear flat or matted, more infill may be needed.
source_label: The Motz Group, How to Get Turf Fibers in Artificial Grass to Stand Up Tall When They're Flat (May 27, 2021)

fact: Motz says flat grass is usually a cosmetic flaw that infill and effort can fix, but that once turf left on low, uneven infill has declined far enough, it cannot be brought all the way back.
quote: While it’s important to stay on top of maintenance and proactively keep your turf from getting matted, a cosmetic flaw like flat grass can be fixed with a little infill and elbow grease. … Low, inconsistent infill levels will leave your outdoor artificial grass looking matted, worn down, and damaged, and unfortunately, once the condition of your turf has declined to a certain point, there’s no getting 100% of its former quality back.
source_label: The Motz Group, How to Get Turf Fibers in Artificial Grass to Stand Up Tall When They're Flat (May 27, 2021)
notes: The source's quoted passages appear in the reverse order on the page (the 'Low, inconsistent infill' paragraph comes first); both are verbatim.

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, a turf distributor, says to check turf in spring for loose seams, lifted edges, broken blades and sagging, and says snow, ice and wind-blown debris can mat blades over weeks or months; its fix is cross-brushing against the grain with a synthetic-bristle broom, never metal prongs.
quote: As spring comes around and the snow finally melts, check your artificial grass for any signs of wear or visible damage. Check for loose seams, lifted edges, broken blades, or sagging surfaces. … Snow, ice, and debris from heavy wind can weigh down your lawn and cause your turf blades to become matted over weeks or months. To help your blades stand upright again, use a broom with synthetic blades to brush the turf against the grain. This technique, known as cross-brushing, will rejuvenate the look of your lawn and help it appear full and lush once more. Any rake or broom will do, but avoid metal prongs which may damage the turf fibers.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, How to Care for Your Artificial Turf in the Spring (Mar. 18, 2021, updated Jan. 9, 2023)

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's Ask JW column says constant foot traffic makes turf fibers lose their memory, that lifting them monthly creates a break line at the infill level that can break fibers off, and recommends concrete, pavers or stepping stones instead of turf at entrances and exits.
quote: I recommend incorporating concrete, pavers or stepping stones in these areas instead of synthetic turf. When heavy foot traffic is continuous it causes the fibers to lose their memory. Trying to uplift the fibers on a monthly basis is not only tiresome but creates a breakline at the infill elevation and may cause the fibers to break and detach.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Premature Matting (2016, updated Dec. 30, 2022)
notes: The column is written for installers; 'these areas' are entrance and exit areas.

fact: The same column says small matted areas can be kept up by hand-dressing them with infill, and that a garden hose left lying on turf presses a depression that is very hard to brush out.
quote: Small areas that are matted could be maintained by hand dressing with infill to keep the fibers vertical. Water hose sitting on synthetic turf can cause a depression and is very hard to brush out. … Keep all water hoses off synthetic turf.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Premature Matting (2016, updated Dec. 30, 2022)

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's Ask JW column says high-traffic areas may need a textured or grooved fiber, and that a smooth fiber may not stand up to heavy wear and will need constant brushing to stay upright.
quote: High traffic areas may require a fiber that is either “textured or grooved”. … If the fiber has no texture or grooves then this fiber may be insufficient for aggressive wear and will create constant maintenance keeping the fibers upright.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Premature Matting (2016, updated Dec. 30, 2022)

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's Ask JW column says most turf fibers are made leaning one way, that brushing them upright can be done by hand with a rake or push broom or with a motorized broom, and that fibers left leaning to one side look shiny because they reflect light.
quote: A majority of manufactures fibers that are tufted lean to one direction when manufactured, some may call this “Turf Lean”. Defibrillation can be done manually with a rake and/or push broom or mechanically with a motorized broom. … When synthetic turf fibers are not brushed vertically and leaning to one side, it creates a shiny appearance. This is due to the reflection of light.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: The Importance of Power Brooms (2016, updated Dec. 29, 2022)

fact: The same column warns that excessive power brooming shortens fiber life, can cause memory loss and premature matting, splits slit-film fibers into thinner strands, and may void the turf's written coverage.
quote: Defibrillation will assist in the maintenance and longevity of the synthetic turf fibers but may also void the warranty of the synthetic turf due to over defibrillation. Over Defibrillation or excessive power brooming can diminish the life of the fibers and may cause memory loss and premature matting. This is especially important for “Slit Film” fibers. Excessive defibrillation on “Slit Film” fibers will cause the fibers to split into thinner fibers and cause premature matting.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: The Importance of Power Brooms (2016, updated Dec. 29, 2022)

fact: The same column describes most power brooms as motorized, string-trimmer-style tools with a brush head, recommends that installers buy or rent one, says some models can be flipped over for gentler grooming, and warns that a hot engine laid on turf can melt the fibers and that fuel should never be added over turf.
quote: I recommend purchasing or renting power brooms if you are wanting to be a successful synthetic turf contractor. There are multiple manufacturers of power brooms. Most power brooms are motorized and look like a “weed eater” with a brush head at the end. … Shindaiwa and Stihl power brooms can be flipped upside down to change the rotation and aggressiveness that is needed for defibrillation. When used in regular position it is very aggressive, when flipped over it is easy on the operator for final grooming. … Power brooms can get hot after long use. Do not lay the power broom on the synthetic turf at any time. The heat from the engine can melt the turf fibers. When adding fuel to the power broom do not add the fuel over the synthetic turf.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: The Importance of Power Brooms (2016, updated Dec. 29, 2022)

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's Ask JW column tells installers not to power broom turf before the infill goes in, because fluffed fibers stop the infill dropping to the backing, and to power broom only after at least eight passes of infill.
quote: When you pre-brush the turf, this prevents the infill from dropping to the base of the turf to ensure complete ballast. … Depending on the face weight, I recommend power-brooming the fibers after at least eight passes of the infill placement.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Don't Power Broom Before Installation (Mar. 31, 2026)

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's Ask JW column recommends maintaining a putting green monthly when it is used for monthly practice, and replenishing infill and rolling putting greens in the spring after snow or winter weather.
quote: If you are using putting greens for monthly practice, I recommend maintaining your putting green surface monthly. I also recommend replenishing and rolling putting greens in the spring after snow fall and/or winter conditions.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Infill Maintenance (Oct. 22, 2020, updated Apr. 2, 2025)

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council's maintenance guidelines for infilled turf say regular brushing keeps infill levels even and fibers upright, and that flattened fibers can speed up wear.
quote: Regular brushing is an important function that must not be overlooked or neglected. Brushing helps to maintain uniform infill levels, keep the grass fibers upright, remove debris, and improve the field appearance. Conversely, the flattening of grass fibers can create a possible acceleration of wear as well as reduced field performance.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Guidelines for Maintenance of Infilled Synthetic Turf Systems (January 2013, Rev. 1)
notes: Written for sports fields; the brushing principles are the ones landscape turf makers repeat for yards.

fact: The STC guidelines assign a brush to level infill and stand fibers up and a mechanical sweeper to remove surface debris, and call for synthetic bristles of the recommended stiffness, never metal or wire bristles.
quote: Use a static brush for general infill leveling and to stand up the grass fibers. A mechanical sweeper or other specialty synthetic turf cleaning equipment should be used to remove surface debris. … Use only synthetic fiber bristles of recommended stiffness. Do not use metal or wire bristles.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Guidelines for Maintenance of Infilled Synthetic Turf Systems (January 2013, Rev. 1)

fact: The STC guidelines say brushing works best when the surface is dry, that high-wear areas have the most pile flattening and need extra attention, that the brushing direction should alternate, that a brush set too low can damage the turf, the seams and the infill, and that excessive brushing damages fibers over time.
quote: It is most effective to brush the surface when it is dry. The high-wear areas will require additional attention as these zones will obviously have the most disrupted infill and pile flattening due to the intensity of play. … The surface should be brushed in a number of directions, alternating the direction in consecutive activities … Do not set the brush so low that it digs into the turf pile or backing. Too low a setting can damage the turf, the seams and disturb the infill. … In general, the frequency will be related to the intensity of use; however, excessive brushing can cause fiber damage which over time will compromise the field’s performance characteristics and longevity.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Guidelines for Maintenance of Infilled Synthetic Turf Systems (January 2013, Rev. 1)
notes: 'longevity' is hyphenated across a line break in the PDF (lon-/gevity), and 'alternating the direction in consecutive activities' runs across the page break between pages 6 and 7.

fact: The STC guidelines say that when blowing small debris off turf, the nozzle should not point straight into the turf and the throttle should be kept low, to keep the infill from moving.
quote: Sunflower seeds, peanut shells, pistachio shells, etc. should be removed as soon as possible by using a hand held or back pack blower. To minimize or eliminate the movement of infill, do not point nozzle directly into the turf. Use minimal throttle to decrease the volume of air.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Guidelines for Maintenance of Infilled Synthetic Turf Systems (January 2013, Rev. 1)

fact: The STC guidelines list fibers that become significantly bent, creased and flat among the conditions that call for comprehensive maintenance, and describe deep cleaning as special equipment that brushes, vacuums and returns the infill.
quote: Grass fibers become significantly bent, creased and flat. … Deep Cleaning—Use special equipment that combines mechanical brushing, suction, and an infill return system to remove surface debris and embedded contaminants.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Guidelines for Maintenance of Infilled Synthetic Turf Systems (January 2013, Rev. 1)

fact: FieldTurf, a sports-turf maker, lists brushing, which it says rejuvenates matted fibers and levels the top of the infill, every 4 to 6 weeks on its fields, and limits grooming machines with rotary brushes to 2 to 3 times a year.
quote: Grooming systems equipped with internal/external rotary brushes should be limited to frequencies of 2-3 times per year. … BRUSHING … Rejuvenates the matted fibers and levels the top portion of the infill. … EVERY 4-6 WEEKS
source_label: FieldTurf, Maintenance Guidelines (April 2017)
notes: The brochure's summary page sets text in columns; the three quoted pieces are separate cells of the same 'Summary of the steps' spread (page 6-7).

fact: FieldTurf says a sweeper's brushes should never reach into the infill; removing debris needs them to touch only the tops of the fibers.
quote: SETTING SWEEPERS: When setting Sweepers for use, make sure that the brushes never penetrate the infill. Proper removal of debris will only require the brushes to penetrate the top of the fibers.
source_label: FieldTurf, Maintenance Guidelines (April 2017)

fact: FieldTurf says a leaf blower used on its fields should be held no closer than 2 feet from the surface and at a 45-degree angle so it doesn't displace infill.
quote: The blower should be held no closer than 2’ from the surface and at a 45 degree angle to avoid displacing any of the infill from the field.
source_label: FieldTurf, Maintenance Guidelines (April 2017)

fact: FieldTurf's emergency repair instructions use a clean shop vacuum on purpose to pull infill out of the turf backing, so it can be reused after the repair.
quote: With the aid of a Shop Vac, making sure that it is clean, as you will re-use the infill, lift the affected area and pull on the turf a bit further in order to insure that the rest of the area is secure. Vacuum the infill from the carpet backing, as well as a bit of infill from each side.
source_label: FieldTurf, Maintenance Guidelines (April 2017)

fact: FieldTurf allows a rotary brush with nylon bristles only for finishing its fields after snow removal, and calls it a delicate job so as not to move or remove too much infill.
quote: A “Rotary Brush” (nylon bristles only) such as found on the Lay-Mor can be used for the final touches, but this is a delicate operation, so as to not move or remove too much infill.
source_label: FieldTurf, Maintenance Guidelines (April 2017)

fact: SYNLawn's DIY installation guidelines say each layer of sand infill is brushed in vigorously with a power broom, Grandi Groomer or coarse nylon broom, across the fibers, and that seams are cross-brushed in both directions to make them less visible.
quote: With each layer of sand, the turf needs to be vigorously brushed using a power broom, Grandi Groomer or coarse bristle nylon broom. The sand will help support the fibers to stand upright. The turf should be brushed across the fibers. … The turf seams should be cross-brushed in both directions. This will make the seams less visible.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (Lowe's product document)

fact: SYNLawn's DIY guidelines recommend a path of stepping stones or pavers where people walk most, to keep the turf from matting and needing more frequent upkeep.
quote: In high traffic paths, we recommend installing a pathway of stepping stone or pavers. This will help prevent the turf from matting down and the need for more frequent maintenance.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (Lowe's product document)

fact: SYNLawn lists brushing and grooming to lift matted areas as part of professional maintenance, and recommends that service once or twice a year for most lawns and quarterly for pet owners, high-traffic areas and commercial properties.
quote: Fiber Rejuvenation: Brushing and grooming to lift matted areas. … We recommend annual or biannual maintenance for most lawns and quarterly service for pet owners, high-traffic areas, and commercial properties.
source_label: SYNLawn, How to Maintain Your Artificial Grass All Year Round (Mar. 1, 2025, updated Sept. 12, 2025)
notes: SYNLawn sells the maintenance service it recommends.

fact: At NOAA's Fort Collins station, March is the snowiest month on average at 9.4 inches, April still averages 6.2 inches and May 1.6 inches, while snow an inch or more deep lies on the ground about 12.3 days in January but only 3.9 days in March and 1.5 in April (1991–2020 normals).
quote: USC00053005 FT COLLINS — MLY-SNOW-NORMAL Jan 6.7 · Feb 7.6 · Mar 9.4 · Apr 6.2 · May 1.6 · MLY-SNWD-AVGNDS-GE001WI Jan 12.3 · Mar 3.9 · Apr 1.5
source_label: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991–2020, monthly, station FT COLLINS (USC00053005)
notes: mly-snow-normal = long-term average monthly snowfall (inches); mly-snwd-avgnds-ge001wi = average number of days in the month with snow depth >= 1 inch (NOAA normals documentation). Station-to-town assignment by proximity, as in climate.json.

fact: At NOAA's Loveland 2N station, February is the snowiest month on average at 8.2 inches, March averages 7.9 inches, April 5.7 and May 1.1, and snow an inch or more deep lies on the ground about 4.4 days in March and 2.3 in April (1991–2020 normals).
quote: USC00055236 LOVELAND 2N — MLY-SNOW-NORMAL Jan 6.0 · Feb 8.2 · Mar 7.9 · Apr 5.7 · May 1.1 · MLY-SNWD-AVGNDS-GE001WI Mar 4.4 · Apr 2.3
source_label: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991–2020, monthly, station LOVELAND 2N (USC00055236)
notes: Element meanings as in matted-artificial-turf.noaa-monthly-snow-fort-collins. Station-to-town assignment by proximity, as in climate.json.

fact: At NOAA's Greeley UNC station, January is the snowiest month on average at 5.7 inches, March averages 5.1 inches, April 3.7 and May 0.5, and snow an inch or more deep lies on the ground about 2.5 days in March and 1.0 in April (1991–2020 normals).
quote: USC00053553 GREELEY UNC — MLY-SNOW-NORMAL Jan 5.7 · Feb 5.1 · Mar 5.1 · Apr 3.7 · May 0.5 · MLY-SNWD-AVGNDS-GE001WI Mar 2.5 · Apr 1.0
source_label: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991–2020, monthly, station GREELEY UNC (USC00053553)
notes: Element meanings as in matted-artificial-turf.noaa-monthly-snow-fort-collins. Station-to-town assignment by proximity, as in climate.json.

fact: Since 2025, Colorado's Regulation 29 has barred local and federal agencies in the state's ozone nonattainment area (local agencies include municipalities, counties, public school districts and special districts), and lawn contractors working for them, from using gasoline-powered push and handheld lawn and garden equipment with engines under 7 kilowatts (10 horsepower) from June 1 to August 31, equipment the state says would otherwise produce about 11% of the ozone-forming emissions in the northern Front Range.
quote: Regulation 29 establishes restrictions on the use of small hand-held lawn and garden equipment between June 1 and August 31, when Colorado typically sees higher ozone pollution levels. If left unregulated, gas-powered lawn and garden equipment could produce around 36 tons of volatile organic compounds per day and 7.5 tons of nitrogen oxides per day in 2026. This accounts for approximately 11% of total air pollution emissions that form ground-level ozone in the northern Front Range of Colorado. … Regulation 29 applies to any local or federal agency that uses small, hand-held lawn and garden equipment within the Colorado ozone pollution nonattainment area. Local agencies include municipalities, county governments, city and county governments, public school districts, and special districts. … Regulation 29 also applies to any lawn-and-garden contractors working for a local or federal agency. Beginning June 1, 2025, covered local and federal agencies cannot use gasoline-powered push and handheld lawn and garden equipment with an internal combustion engine smaller than 7 kilowatt (10 horsepower) from June 1 to August 31 of the current year.
source_label: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, Lawn and garden equipment requirements (Regulation 29)
notes: The page's examples of covered equipment include leaf blowers, dethatchers and power washers and cover 'any piece of equipment that has the primary purpose of assisting with the cleanup or maintenance of the lawn or garden area of a property'; power brooms are not named. Whether a power broom is covered is our reading, not the state's. Re-check after the November 2026 Air Quality Control Commission hearing (see matted-artificial-turf.cdphe-reg29-commercial-hearing).

fact: In November 2026 Colorado's Air Quality Control Commission will consider extending Regulation 29's summertime restrictions to commercial lawn and garden equipment; the state defines push and handheld lawn equipment as any tool whose main purpose is cleaning up or maintaining a property's lawn or garden area.
quote: July 2026 update: In November 2026, the Air Quality Control Commission will consider revising state Regulation 29 to expand the summertime equipment use restrictions to commercial lawn and garden equipment. … Push and hand-held lawn and garden equipment can be any piece of equipment that has the primary purpose of assisting with the cleanup or maintenance of the lawn or garden area of a property.
source_label: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, Lawn and garden equipment requirements (Regulation 29)
notes: Proposed, not adopted, as of 2026-09-25. After the November hearing, record what the commission decided and when any commercial restriction starts.

fact: CDPHE says the state's ozone nonattainment area under the 2015 federal standard takes in the northern Front Range, including northern Weld County, which the EPA reclassified from moderate to serious nonattainment in July 2024.
quote: In July 2024, the EPA approved the state’s voluntary request to update its nonattainment classification for the 2015 standard. This update reclassified the … northern Front Range, including northern Weld County, from a “moderate” to a “serious'' nonattainment area.
source_label: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, Nonattainment and federal ozone pollution standards
notes: The elided words are the first half of the area's name, which names the metro area to the south; NoCo copy never names it. The page does not list which parts of Larimer County are inside the area, so copy tells readers to confirm by address.
